title: Precompiling Build-Time Secrets
pattern: Injecting operational passwords, keys, or endpoints during compilation via environment-based preprocessor macros or build scripts.
why_bad: Couples the compiled binary irrevocably to a single operational target. It prevents deploying the same binary across multiple environments (dev, staging, prod), breaking continuous delivery principles.
detection: The presence of compile-time environment capture macros (such as `env!` or `option_env!` in Rust) targeting sensitive credentials.
fix: Resolve secrets dynamically at runtime through file loaders, environment variables, or secure external agents, keeping binaries strictly environment-agnostic.
source: Heather Adkins et al., - *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 14.
